idea: A website where my gym friends log workouts and see a weekly leaderboard

result.restatement: A website where gym friends log workouts and see a weekly leaderboard.

decisions.question: How should workout entries be stored and leaderboard scores calculated?
decisions.choice: Workout entries live in a database table with columns for user, exercise, weight, reps, and date, and the leaderboard is computed by querying that table each week.
decisions.why: The idea requires saving many workouts and ranking users weekly, which a database handles reliably; any device can reach it through the website.
decisions.tradeoffs: A database is more complex than a single file but avoids data loss and makes weekly ranking fast.

alternatives.name: JSON file
alternatives.betterWhen: Only one person uses it and data never needs to scale.

alternatives.name: Spreadsheet
alternatives.betterWhen: You want zero setup and do not need automatic weekly ranking.

decisions.question: What runs in the browser to show the log form and leaderboard?
decisions.choice: HTML, CSS, and JavaScript files that load in any browser and call the server to save or read workouts.
decisions.why: Your friends use different phones and laptops; a website opens on all of them without installing anything.
decisions.tradeoffs: Simple and cheap, but interactivity requires JavaScript and API calls instead of just HTML.

alternatives.name: Mobile app
alternatives.betterWhen: You want native phone features and are willing to build for iOS and Android.

alternatives.name: Desktop app
alternatives.betterWhen: Users only ever use one computer and do not need phones.

decisions.question: How does the browser send a new workout to the server?
decisions.choice: A server endpoint receives workout data over HTTP and writes it to the database.
decisions.why: The frontend and database are separate, so they need a defined way to talk over the web.
decisions.tradeoffs: Adds a small server layer, but keeps the frontend simple and secure.

alternatives.name: Direct database access
alternatives.betterWhen: You are building a local tool with no browser and no security concerns.

alternatives.name: File upload
alternatives.betterWhen: You only need to import bulk data once and never query it live.

decisions.question: Where does the website and server run so friends can access it?
decisions.choice: The static site and API run on a cloud platform reachable by anyone with the link.
decisions.why: Friends need to use it from their own devices, so it must be online and not just on your laptop.
decisions.tradeoffs: Costs a little and requires an account, but removes the need to keep your computer on.

alternatives.name: Your own computer
alternatives.betterWhen: Only you will use it and you can leave your laptop running.

alternatives.name: Local network
alternatives.betterWhen: All friends are on the same Wi-Fi and you do not need internet access.

decisions.question: How do you know which friend logged which workout?
decisions.choice: Each friend creates an account with email and password, and workouts are saved under that account.
decisions.why: The leaderboard must attribute workouts to the right person, so the app needs to identify users.
decisions.tradeoffs: Adds sign-up and login screens, but prevents friends from editing each other's entries.

alternatives.name: No sign-in
alternatives.betterWhen: Only one person uses the app and no attribution is needed.

alternatives.name: OAuth
alternatives.betterWhen: You want friends to log in with Google or Apple and not create a new password.

firstSteps: Create a folder for the project and open it in a code editor.
Write one HTML page with a form to enter exercise, weight, reps, and date.
Set up a database table with columns for user, exercise, weight, reps, and date.
Build one API route that receives the form data and saves a row to the table.
Add a second page that queries the table and shows a weekly leaderboard sorted by total weight.
Deploy the site and API to cloud hosting and share the link with friends.
result.agentsMd:
# AGENTS.md

## What this is
A website where gym friends log workouts and see a weekly leaderboard.

## Stack
- Static site: HTML, CSS and JavaScript
- A small server with API routes
- A database with a schema (for example PostgreSQL)
- Cloud hosting

## Structure
- /src - server code and API routes
- /public - HTML, CSS, and browser JavaScript
- /db - database schema and seed file

## How to work
- Build one small step at a time. Explain the plan before changing many files.
- Commit after every working change with a clear message.
- Ask before adding a dependency. Prefer none.
- If something fails, say so plainly. Do not hide it.

## Rules
- Never trust data from the browser; validate exercise, weight, reps, and date before saving.
- Keep database logic in server files, not in browser JavaScript.
- Use environment variables for database credentials and never commit them.
- Return clear error messages when a workout is missing required fields.
- Log every API request and database error to help debug problems.

## Security
- Never commit secrets. Keep them in a gitignored env file and in the host's secret store.
- API keys (for an AI model or any paid service) live only on a server or serverless function, never in browser code. If the plan has no backend, add the smallest one that can hold the key, and say so.
- Validate all input. Never put user text into the page with innerHTML.
